steps.title: Find the quotes and the Fact Find (three routes), name the funds, fetch each fund's current fact sheet, and register everything
do: Find the documents the page below lists in the client's own folders. Try the routes IN THIS ORDER and record EVERY try, failures too:
1  device: the computer (local drive / OneDrive)    2  m365: the Microsoft 365 connector    3  zapier: the Zapier Office 365 tools
Record each try: python3 {scripts}/run.py access {run} --purpose locate --route device|m365|zapier --result failed|found --note "what you did"
Register each quote (one per provider, the label is the provider's name) and the Fact Find: python3 {scripts}/run.py doc {run} --role quote --label "Provider" --file <local copy> --route <the route>

Name every fund shown on the quotes: python3 {scripts}/run.py funds {run} --file funds.json (the program refuses a fund that is not in its provider's quote). Then fetch EACH fund's CURRENT fact sheet from the web (the search and fetch tools first, then Claude in Chrome; log every try with --purpose factsheet), SAVE the sheet's text in a file and register it. The program prints the exact commands.
Every optional document is registered or confirmed not to exist with Paul's words (`--missing`). The quotes can never be missing: STOP and ask Paul.
Show Paul the 'what I found' list (one line per document: file name, date, folder or web address, and anything missing, conflicting or unreadable) in your reply.
steps.proof: the tries are logged in order, two or more quotes are registered, the Fact Find is registered or accounted for, every named fund has its fact sheet (or Paul's words)

steps.title: Read the registered documents, one page at a time
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py read {run}

The program shows the text page by page. Read each page fully, then acknowledge it with a one-line note (`run.py read {run} --ack KEY:PAGE --note "..."`). Pages are acknowledged in order; a page with no readable text must be viewed as an image by you.
steps.proof: every page was served in order and acknowledged

steps.title: Enter the answers with their sources; the program checks every figure against the documents
do: Write ONE answers file in the layout the page below describes, every answer with its source, then run: python3 {scripts}/run.py answers {run} --file <your answers file>

The program refuses a fee, premium, term, fund, allocation, loyalty figure, fund-sheet figure or date it cannot find in the right document's text, allocations that do not add up to 100%, a quote that shows only a blended cost (EAC), a quote that is not the product being compared, a fund description copied from the fact sheet, a conflict between sources (then STOP and ask Paul).

Ask Paul for what only he can give: which extras he wants (tax note, flexibility, a fees-only comparison and its example fund value), the meetings already held and the next meeting. Never type a figure from memory and never copy one from another client.
steps.proof: the answers are valid, sourced, free of conflicts, and every figure was found in the right document's text

steps.title: The program works out the comparison: apples-to-apples, fee totals, Tax-Free room, stale or missing fact sheets
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py check {run}

Read what it prints. A mismatch between the quotes (contribution structure, amount, yearly increase or term) is NOT a like-for-like comparison: do not go on unless Paul says so (the confirmation table asks him). Nothing is typed or adjusted by you.
steps.proof: the comparison was worked out by the program from these answers

steps.title: Show Paul the confirmation table, ask ONE question, record his yes
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py show {run}

Put the whole table it prints in your reply (it includes the comparison, the flags, the email subject and the exact Teams message to Sitamah) and ask exactly the one question it gives. Nothing is built before his clear yes.
When he says yes, record his own words: python3 {scripts}/run.py approve {run} --said "his exact words"
If an answer changes, run answers and check again and show again: the earlier yes then no longer counts.
steps.proof: Paul was shown exactly these answers and results and said yes

steps.title: The program fills the fixed template and builds the email, the saved copy and the text for the draft
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py build {run}

It fills the template from your confirmed answers (never typed): the four tables in the fixed order, the plain-English intro lines, the 'Things to know' box only when something must be flagged, the optional parts only if Paul asked, every weekday, every total. It checks the result. You never edit a script, the template or the HTML.
Send the full copy (with the logo) to Paul in the chat with the exact file name the program gives.
steps.proof: the three files are exactly what the program builds from the confirmed answers and pass the program's checks

steps.title: Save the no-logo copy in the client's Comparative Quotes folder, never overwriting without Paul's yes
do: List the client's folder for this product > `Comparative Quotes` (computer first, then Microsoft 365, then Zapier; record every try with --purpose save) and note the file names already there. Then: python3 {scripts}/run.py name {run} --existing "name one.html;name two.html"
If a file with the same name exists the program stops: ask Paul; only with his yes run it again with --overwrite-yes "his words".
Save exactly the file it names (the no-logo copy; never retype or truncate the logo). If the folder does not exist, ask Paul. List the folder again and record what it shows:
python3 {scripts}/run.py receipt {run} save.folder <the folder path>   save.listed_bytes <the html's size in the listing>
Tell Paul in plain words that the saved copy has no logo (the Outlook draft gets Paul's signature and logo separately).
steps.proof: the derived name was used, nothing was overwritten without Paul's yes, the folder is Comparative Quotes and the listed size equals the local file

steps.title: Make the Outlook draft with Claude in Chrome (never sent by Claude) and read it back for the program
do: Follow the page below. The text to paste is the draft_body.html the program built. Read the saved draft back, save the read-back to a file and run: python3 {scripts}/run.py draft {run} --file <the saved read-back>
Every line must be a green tick. Then record the cleanup: run.py receipt {run} draft.tab_closed yes   run.py receipt {run} draft.stray_deleted <number or none>
steps.proof: the saved read-back of the draft passes every program check and the cleanup is recorded

steps.title: Message Sitamah on Teams through Zapier (the wording is the program's) and read the posted message back
do: Look in the 1:1 chat for whether the same time-of-day greeting was already used today by Paul or Claude, then run: python3 {scripts}/run.py message {run} --used-today yes|no

Send exactly the message it prints, as it says. Read the posted message back, save it to a file, record the receipts it names and run: python3 {scripts}/run.py messagecheck {run} --file <the saved read-back>
steps.proof: the message went to the 1:1 chat as markdown and its read-back passes every program check

steps.title: The final check and the SHORT AUDIT for Paul
do: Run: python3 {scripts}/run.py done {run} final
Put in your reply, as it is: where the copy was saved, the draft's status, that Sitamah was messaged, then the short audit. Nothing longer.
Any red cross means the job is not finished: say so.
steps.proof: the final checker prints no red cross
